the use of a multimodal, real-time, experiential media biofeedback system for rehabilitation of patients with stroke has the potential to improve the quality of the therapy and to provide a more effective means of rehabilitation.
we have successfully integrated the task-dependent physical therapy and cognitive stimulation within a multimodal environment that provides a purposeful and engaging visual and auditory scene.
we have developed a real-time, multimodel biofeedback system for the rehabilitation of stroke patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an experiential, multimodal, real-time, biofeedback system for functional rehabilitation therapy.
the design, development and evaluation of a novel, real-time, multimodality biofeedback system for the purpose of stroke patient rehabilitation.

the design of interactive systems that can provide a rich, engaging, multimodal environment for stroke patients, while providing detailed, real-time, quantitative measures of performance and progress for the patient, the therapist, and the physician.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed an interactive multimodal system that is able to provide real-time, multimodel feedback that is both informative and motivating for the user.

the system is a novel and effective means of providing biofeedback in a manner that is more engaging than traditional rehabilitation methods, and is more effective at providing a quantitative measure of recovery than traditional clinical methods.
we have successfully developed a real-time biofeedback system that is able to provide a multimodal, task specific, real time feedback to stroke patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a real-time, multi modal biofeedback system for rehabilitation of stroke patients that is capable of delivering a wide range of feedback to the patient in a real-time environment.
we have developed a novel, multimodal, interactive system that provides a rich and dynamic environment that engages the patient in a task that requires both physical and cognitive abilities.

the system has the ability to provide real-time, multi-sensory, multimodal feedback to patients in a way that is task specific, and that the system is designed in such a way as to be easily extensible to other tasks and modalities.

the system provides a rich environment for the stroke patient to interact and practice in a way that is engaging and meaningful.
the use of multimodal feedback is a powerful mechanism to improve the quality and quantity of rehabilitation.
the design of the task is crucial in the design of a biofeedback system for rehabilitation.
